title: Nepal's July foreign tourist arrivals edge up - The Star
description: Nepal's July foreign tourist arrivals edge up  The Star
publisher.title: The Star
full_article:
KATHMANDU: Foreign tourist arrivals to Nepal increased by 2.3 percent in July compared with the same month last year, driven mainly by a sharp rise in visitors from China and the United States, according to Nepal Tourism Board.

The board said in its monthly report released on Monday that Nepal welcomed 71,775 international traveler visits in July, up from 70,193 arrivals recorded during the same month in 2025.

Even as Indian tourists continued to account for the largest share of foreign visitors, with 23,490 arrivals during the month, the number declined compared to the same period last year, according to the board. - Xinhua

Proton e.MAS 5 is now officially available in Nepal, which is the EV’s 2nd international market after Singapore. The electric hatchback is also the 2nd Proton e.MAS model in Nepal after the e.MAS 7, which was launched there in March 2025.

Proton e.MAS 5 Nepal Pricing, Warranty

Just like Malaysia, Proton e.MAS 5 can be obtained in two variants over in Nepal. Here’s the launch promotional price for the EV over there for the first 100 customers:

Proton e.MAS 5 Prime: NPR29.99 lakh (~RM80,802)

NPR29.99 lakh (~RM80,802) Proton e.MAS 5 Premium: NPR34.99 lakh (~RM94,274)

The standard price for the e.MAS 5 in Nepal is NPR32.99 lakh (~RM88,896) for the Prime variant, while the Premium version costs NPR36.99 lakh (~RM99,674).

Similar to Malaysia, the e.MAS 5 in Nepal comes with a 6-year unlimited mileage warranty. There is a separate 8-year / 160,000km warranty for the car’s high-voltage battery and components.

Proton e.MAS 5 Quick Specs

Proton e.MAS 5 Jade Green was launched at Penang Autoshow 2026.

In general, the specifications of the Proton e.MAS 5 for the Nepalese market is similar to Malaysia. This include all 6 colourways that are available over here such as Marble Cream, Graphite Silver, Slate Grey, Moonstone White, Quartz Rose, and the newly released Jade Green.

Powered by a 40.16kWh LFP battery, the high-spec e.MAS 5 Premium features an 85kW (114hp) motor with 150Nm of torque. The Premium variant is also capable of delivering a WLTP-rated range of 325km.

On the other hand, there is the e.MAS 5 Prime, which is equipped with a 30.12kWh LFP battery alongside a 58kW (78hp) motor with 130Nm of torque. Given its smaller battery capacity, the Prime variant’s range is also much lower at 225km, according to WLTP standards.

In terms of charging, the e.MAS 5 Premium supports DC charging speed of up to 71kW and takes 21 minutes to charge from 30% to 80%. The e.MAS 5 Prime also has the same charging duration even though its DC charging speed is much lower at 53kW.

Both e.MAS 5 variants are equipped with a 6.6kW 1-phase AC onboard charger. It takes around 4.3 hours to charge the e.MAS 5 Prime from 10% to 100% via AC charging, while the e.MAS 5 Premium takes slightly longer at 5.9 hours since it has a larger battery.

Other features that are exclusive to the Premium variant include 16-inch alloy wheels, a 360-degree camera, LED headlights, and a powered tailgate. The Premium variant also has an Advanced Driver Assistance System (ADAS) that covers features such as Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC), Autonomous Emergency Braking (AEB), Forward & Rear Collision Warning (FCW/RCW), Lane Change Assist (LCA), Blind Spot Detection (BSD), and many more.

There are still many features that both e.MAS Premium and Prime share, including 70L frunk, 28L rear underseat storage space, 375L to 1320L of boot space, 14.6-inch full HD infotainment display with Atlas Auto operating system, Android Auto & Apple CarPlay support, integrated live EV charging map, Proton e.MAS App support, leatherette seats, rear-wheel drive setup, and rear multi-link suspension.

description: Nepal records 2.3pc rise in July tourist arrivals despite monsoon season  The Himalayan Times
publisher.title: The Himalayan Times
full_article:
KATHMANDU, AUGUST 3

Nepal welcomed 71,775 international visitors in July, posting a 2.3 per cent year-on-year increase despite the monsoon season, according to the Nepal Tourism Board (NTB).

Related Articles Nepal welcomes over 91,000 foreign tourists in June, up 19.5% year-on-year Nepal's first NEC-accredited CPD Training on contract management concludes in Kathmandu

The latest figures show Nepal received 71,775 international visitor arrivals (IVAs) in July 2026, compared with 70,193 arrivals during the same month last year.

India remained Nepal's largest source market, contributing 23,490 visitors or 32.73 per cent of total arrivals. China ranked second with 11,099 visitors (15.46 per cent), followed by the United States with 7,754 (10.80 per cent), Bangladesh with 4,179 (5.82 per cent), and the United Kingdom with 3,773 visitors (5.26 per cent).

Visitors from other regions made up 3.9 per cent of arrivals, with the Middle East and Africa contributing 1.0 per cent and 0.5 per cent, respectively.

The Nepal Tourism Board said the July figures reflected continued international interest in Nepal and growing momentum in positioning the country as a lifetime travel destination.

full_article:
Mumbai — Bollywood actress Shilpa Shetty shared a glimpse of her visit to Nepal’s Pashupatinath Temple, posting a photograph from the revered Hindu shrine.

In the image, Shetty is seen wearing a bright yellow traditional outfit and standing with her hands folded in prayer in front of the temple.

“@pashupatinath temple #nepaldiaries,” she wrote in the caption.

Located along the Bagmati River in Kathmandu, Pashupatinath Temple is dedicated to Pashupati, a form of Shiva. The temple complex is among South Asia’s most prominent Hindu religious sites and forms part of the Kathmandu Valley UNESCO World Heritage Site.

The complex includes hundreds of smaller shrines surrounding its principal pagoda-style temple.

Shetty was most recently seen in the Kannada-language action thriller “KD: The Devil,” directed by Prem. The film also stars Dhruva Sarja, Sanjay Dutt, V. Ravichandran, Ramesh Aravind, Reeshma Nanaiah, Jisshu Sengupta and Nora Fatehi.

She is also hosting the reality cooking series “Maa Hai Na,” in which celebrity contestants compete in pairs with a parent or adult child in cooking challenges and comedy segments.

Shetty made her film debut in the 1993 thriller “Baazigar” and later appeared in movies including “Main Khiladi Tu Anari” and “Jaanwar.”

The actress recently denied social media statements about India’s reservation system that had been falsely attributed to her, calling them fabricated and malicious.

“I am shocked to see fake statements on reservation falsely attached to my name,” she wrote. “This is completely fabricated, malicious garbage. Do not fall for this fake news!” (Source: IANS)

title: Nepal raises dismantling of Susta earthen barrier with New Delhi - The Kathmandu Post
description: Nepal raises dismantling of Susta earthen barrier with New Delhi  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
The Nepali Embassy in New Delhi on Sunday formally raised with India’s Ministry of External Affairs an incident in which Indian security personnel crossed into Nepali territory in Susta in Nawalparasi West and dismantled a mud embankment built by local villagers to protect their village from flooding.

The embassy raised the issue on the same day of the incident.

“Our officials protested the way Indian security personnel dismantled the makeshift embankment,” said a foreign ministry official, adding, “We told them that it was a last-resort effort by locals to mitigate flooding.”

Susta and Kalapani are two major boundary disputes between Nepal and India, with both sides acknowledging them as contested areas. In 2014, both sides agreed that the issue would be resolved through the mechanism involving foreign secretaries and the Boundary Working Group. However, in the past 12 years, no meeting at the foreign secretary level has been held to address the dispute.

According to two officials at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Indian side insisted that Susta and where the Nepali side is building the mud dam are disputed territories and that both sides had agreed to maintain the status quo.

A similar dispute erupted two months ago when India's SSB personnel halted the construction of a permanent flood-control embankment being built by the Nepal government in the same area. Following a minor scuffle at the time, officials from Nepal’s Armed Police Force (AFP) and India’s SSB reached an agreement to maintain the status quo, stating that Susta is a mutually agreed disputed area.

On Sunday also, the Indian side reiterated the same position, calling the area disputed and saying no new structure could be constructed there, according to the two officials.

Besides regular meetings between the security agencies, the chief district officer and district magistrate of the Indian side do sit regularly if any dispute arises along the border.

Dipak Nepal, the chief district officer of Nawalparasi West, told the Post that the situation was normal on Monday.

As soon as Nepali media reported the matter on Sunday, the Nepali Embassy in New Delhi took it up with the Indian side, seeking a prompt resolution. However, the Indian side called for restraint and said the issue should not be turned into a national agenda.

The dispute intensified after Nepal awarded a contract to construct a 132-metre flood-protection embankment along the Narayani River. According to local officials, the project could not proceed after the Indian side raised objections, leaving the entire stretch without permanent protection. They said Nepal has already completed embankment construction downstream of the 132-metre section, while the disputed stretch remains the only unprotected gap.

Since then, the exposed riverbank has continued to suffer severe erosion caused by the Narayani River. Local residents say they attempted to build temporary protective structures to mitigate the immediate risk of flooding, but those efforts were also halted, despite the works being carried out within Nepali territory and outside the disputed section.

Officials and local communities warn that the unprotected stretch has become one of the main entry points for monsoon floodwaters into Susta. They maintain that Nepal’s objective in constructing the embankment is to protect its territory, farmland and settlements from river erosion and flooding. As Indian territory lies both upstream and downstream of this section of the river, some local officials also believe that coordinated embankment and river-training works on both sides would be necessary for effective flood management.

In the absence of protective measures, they say, riverbank erosion continues to reduce the area of Nepali land in Susta year after year.

On Sunday, according to locals, a group of Indian security personnel in plain clothes entered Nepali territory carrying spades and began digging up the mud embankment that villagers had recently built to reduce the risk of floodwaters from the Narayani river inundating the settlement.

Residents rushed to stop them, triggering a standoff before Nepal’s Armed Police Force intervened to prevent the situation from escalating.

Later as per the past agreement, APF and SSB personnel quickly brought the situation under control.

On 8 December 1988 Nepal and India agreed to treat the Narayani River as a boundary river under the principle of a fixed boundary, according to former Director General Buddhi Narayan Shrestha.

Under this principle, the boundary remains fixed as it existed when the Nepal-India boundary agreement was signed, he added.

“Fixed boundary principle applies to the demarcation of the riverine sector of Tarai lowlands. It requires identifying the river’s course as it existed at the time of the agreement and demarcating the boundary by placing alternative pillars on both sides of the river, regardless of whether water or river channel exists there today. This principle was adopted as per the decision of Nepal government on 8 December 1988 and agreed upon by both countries,” said Shrestha.

However, over the last several decades, the Narayani River has changed course, creating complications over land ownership and leading to competing claims in the area.

Rabindra Jaiswal, spokesperson for the Susta Protection Campaign, said villagers had constructed the temporary earthen embankment only after Indian authorities blocked them from building a permanent flood-control structure along the Narayani River.

While 16 border pillars mark most of the Nepal-India boundary in Nawalparasi West, there are no boundary pillars along the roughly 24-kilometre Susta stretch.

Instead, the two countries rely on natural features such as rivers and trees to mark the boundary. As a result disputes over land ownership and cultivation recur frequently. A silk cotton tree currently serves as the de facto boundary marker in part of the disputed area.

Residents say the changing course of the Narayani river over the decades has further complicated the border.

Sunday’s incident followed a similar dispute on May 31, when India’s SSB entered ward 5 of Susta Rural Municipality and objected to the construction of a permanent embankment being built by Nepal’s Ministry of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation.

According to Chief District Officer Nepal, the dispute centred on a new 132-metre section of embankment planned about 50 metres to the east of an existing structure, still within Nepali territory.

The project was initiated after then energy minister Kulman Ghising visited Susta about eight months ago and directed authorities to prioritise flood protection for the vulnerable settlement.

Susta is bounded by the Narayani river to the north and west and India’s Bihar state to the south and east.

India maintains three SSB outposts near the area, while Nepal has an APF border post commanded by an inspector.

Residents say Indian authorities have repeatedly objected to Nepal’s activities in the area, citing the absence of clearly demarcated border pillars.

Two weeks ago, 52 residents led by Susta campaigner Munna Khan travelled to Kathmandu and staged a protest at Maitighar Mandala, demanding stronger state protection.

During a meeting with Home Minister Sudan Gurung, they urged the government to establish a Nepali Army security post in Susta, alleging years of harassment by Indian security personnel.

Following the meeting, the home ministry instructed the district administration to reinforce security in sensitive areas of Susta and to begin processing citizenship applications for eligible residents who lack citizenship documents.

नई दिल्ली स्थित नेपाली दूतावास रविदिन भारत के विदेश मंत्रालय के संग औपचारिक रूप सं एकटा एहन घटना के जानकारी देलक जाहि मे भारतीय सुरक्षाकर्मी नवलपरासी पश्चिम के सुस्ता मे नेपाली इलाका पार क अपन गाम के बाढ़ि सं बचाबय लेल स्थानीय ग्रामीण द्वारा बनाओल गेल माटिक तटबंध के तोड़ि देलक.

दूतावास घटनाक ओही दिन मुद्दा उठौलक।

विदेश मंत्रालय केरऽ एगो अधिकारी न॑ कहलकै कि हमरऽ अधिकारी न॑ भारतीय सुरक्षाकर्मी न॑ अस्थायी तटबंध क॑ तोड़ै के तरीका के विरोध करलकै आरू कहलकै कि हम्में हुनका सब क॑ कहल॑ छेलियै कि ई स्थानीय लोगऽ के बाढ़ क॑ कम करै के अंतिम प्रयास छेकै ।

सुस्ता आ कालापानी नेपाल आ भारतक बीच दूटा प्रमुख सीमा विवाद अछि, जाहिमे दुनू पक्ष एकरा प्रतिस्पर्धी क्षेत्रक रूपमे स्वीकार केने अछि । 2014 मे दुनू पक्ष एहि बात पर सहमत भेल छल जे विदेश सचिव आ सीमा कार्यदल कए शामिल करय वाला तंत्र क माध्यम स एहि मुद्दा क समाधान होएत। मुदा पिछला 12 साल मे एहि विवाद कए दूर करबा लेल विदेश सचिव स्तर पर कोनो बैसार नहि भेल अछि।

विदेश मन्त्रालयके दूटा अधिकारीके अनुसार भारतीय पक्ष सुस्ता आ नेपाली पक्ष जतए माटिक बाँध बना रहल अछि ओ विवादित क्षेत्र रहल आ दुनु पक्ष यथास्थिति कायम राखयके सहमतिमे रहल जिद्द केलक अछि ।

दू मास पहिने एहने विवाद तखन उठल छल जखन भारतक एसएसबी के जवान नेपाल सरकार द्वारा ओही इलाका मे बनाओल जा रहल स्थायी बाढ़ नियंत्रण तटबंध के निर्माण बंद क देलक। ओहि समय एकटा छोट सन झगड़ा के बाद नेपाल के सशस्त्र पुलिस बल (एएफपी) आ भारत के एसएसबी के अधिकारी सब यथास्थिति के कायम रखबाक लेल समझौता पर पहुंच गेल आ कहल गेल जे सुस्ता आपसी सहमत विवादित क्षेत्र अछि।

रविदिन सेहो भारतीय पक्ष सेहो इएह रुख दोहराबैत एहि इलाका कए विवादित बतौलक आ कहलक जे ओतय कोनो नव संरचना नहि बनाउल जा सकैत अछि, दुनू अधिकारी क अनुसार।

सुरक्षा एजेंसी के बीच नियमित बैठक के अलावा भारतीय पक्ष के मुख्य जिला अधिकारी आरू जिला मजिस्ट्रेट अगर सीमा के किनारे कोनो विवाद पैदा होय जाय छै त नियमित रूप स॑ जरूर बैठै छै ।

नवलपरासी पश्चिमके प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारी दिपक नेपाल सोमदिन स्थिति सामान्य रहल पोस्टके बतौलनि ।

रविदिन नेपाली मीडिया जहिना एहि विषयक खबरि देलक तहिना नई दिल्ली मे नेपाली दूतावास भारतीय पक्षक संग एकरा शीघ्र समाधानक मांग केलक। हालांकि भारतीय पक्ष संयम के आह्वान करैत कहलक जे एहि मुद्दा के राष्ट्रीय एजेंडा मे नहि बदलल जाय।

नेपाल द्वारा नारायणी नदीक कात मे 132 मीटर बाढ़ि सुरक्षा तटबंध बनेबाक ठेका देलाक बाद विवाद तेज भ गेल। स्थानीय अधिकारी के अनुसार भारतीय पक्ष के आपत्ति के बाद ई परियोजना आगू नै बढ़ि सकल, जाहि स पूरा हिस्सा स्थायी सुरक्षा के बिना रहि गेल। ओ सब कहलनि जे, नेपाल 132 मीटर के खण्ड के नीचा तटबंध निर्माण पूरा क चुकल अछि, जखन कि विवादित खंड एकमात्र असुरक्षित अंतर बनल अछि।

तहिया सँ उजागर नदी तट पर नारायणी नदीक कारण भयंकर कटाव होइत रहल अछि । स्थानीय निवासी के कहनाय छनि जे बाढ़ि के तत्काल खतरा कम करय लेल अस्थायी सुरक्षा संरचना बनेबाक प्रयास केलखिन्ह, मुदा ओ प्रयास सेहो रोकल गेल छल, जखन कि नेपाली इलाका के भीतर आओर विवादित खंड के बाहर काज भ रहल छल.

अधिकारी आरू स्थानीय समुदाय चेतावनी दै छै कि ई असुरक्षित हिस्सा मानसून के बाढ़ के पानी लेली सुस्ता म॑ मुख्य प्रवेश बिंदु म॑ स॑ एक बनी गेलऽ छै । हुनकऽ कहना छै कि तटबंध केरऽ निर्माण म॑ नेपाल केरऽ उद्देश्य अपनऽ इलाका, खेती के जमीन आरू बस्ती क॑ नदी केरऽ कटाव आरू बाढ़ स॑ बचाना छै । जेना कि भारतीय इलाका नदी केरऽ ई भाग केरऽ ऊपर आरू नीचे दोनों तरफ छै, ई लेली कुछ स्थानीय अधिकारी सिनी के ई भी मानना ​​छै कि प्रभावी बाढ़ प्रबंधन लेली दोनों तरफ समन्वित तटबंध आरू नदी-प्रशिक्षण के काम जरूरी होतै ।

सुरक्षा उपाय के अभाव में नदी के कात के कटाव स साल दर साल सुस्ता में नेपाली भूमि के क्षेत्रफल में कमी जारी रहैत अछि, हुनकर कहनाय छनि।

रविदिन स्थानीय लोकक अनुसार सादा वस्त्र मे भारतीय सुरक्षाकर्मीक समूह कुदाल लऽ कऽ नेपाली क्षेत्र मे प्रवेश कए गामक लोक सभ हालहि मे बनल माटिक तटबंध खोदब शुरू केलक जाहि सँ नारायणी नदी सँ बाढ़िक पानि बस्ती मे डूबबाक खतरा कम भ' जाय।

निवासी सब हुनका सब के रोकय लेल दौड़ल, जाहि सं नेपाल के सशस्त्र पुलिस बल के हस्तक्षेप सं पहिने स्थिति बढ़य सं रोकल गेल.

बाद मे पिछला समझौता क अनुसार एपीएफ आ एसएसबी क जवान जल्दीए स्थिति पर काबू पाबि लेलथि।

पूर्व महानिदेशक बुद्धि नारायण श्रेष्ठ के अनुसार ८ दिसम्बर १९८८ के नेपाल आ भारत नारायणी नदी के निश्चित सीमा के सिद्धांत के तहत सीमा नदी के रूप में मानय पर सहमत भेल छल ।

एहि सिद्धांत मे नेपाल-भारत सीमा सम्झौता पर हस्ताक्षर भेला पर सीमा जेना छल तेना स्थिर अछि, ओ आगू कहलनि ।

“तराई तराई केरऽ नदी क्षेत्र केरऽ सीमांकन प॑ निश्चित सीमा सिद्धांत लागू होय छै । एकरा लेली नदी केरऽ मार्ग के पहचान करना जरूरी छै जेना कि समझौता के समय मौजूद छेलै आरू नदी केरऽ दोनों तरफ वैकल्पिक खंभा लगाय क॑ सीमा के सीमांकन करना जरूरी छै, चाहे आज वहाँ पानी होय या नदी के चैनल मौजूद होय । ई सिद्धान्त नेपाल सरकारके ८ दिसम्बर १९८८के निर्णय अनुसार अपनाओल गेल आ दुनु देशके सहमति भेल छल ।’ श्रेष्ठ बतौलनि ।

लेकिन पिछला कई दशक स॑ नारायणी नदी केरऽ रास्ता बदली गेलऽ छै, जेकरा स॑ जमीन केरऽ मालिकाना हक प॑ जटिलता पैदा होय गेलऽ छै आरू ई क्षेत्र म॑ प्रतिस्पर्धी दावा पैदा होय गेलऽ छै ।

सुस्ता संरक्षण अभियान के प्रवक्ता रवीन्द्र जायसवाल नँ कहलकै कि भारतीय अधिकारियौ नँ नारायणी नदी के किनारे स्थायी बाढ़ नियंत्रण संरचना बनाबै मँ रोकला के बाद ही ग्रामीणौ अस्थायी माटी के तटबंध के निर्माण करलकै ।

नवलपरासी पश्चिम में नेपाल-भारत सीमा के अधिकांश भाग के 16 सीमा खंभा चिन्हित करैत अछि, मुदा मोटा-मोटी 24 किलोमीटर लंबा सुस्ता खंड में कोनो सीमा खंभा नै अछि।

बल्कि दुनू देश सीमा चिन्हित करय लेल नदी आ गाछ जेहन प्राकृतिक विशेषता पर निर्भर अछि । परिणामस्वरूप जमीनक मालिकाना हक आ खेती पर विवाद बेर-बेर होइत अछि । एक रेशम कपास के गाछ वर्तमान में विवादित क्षेत्र के कुछ हिस्सा में वास्तविक सीमा चिह्न के रूप में काम करै छै.

निवासी सब के कहनाय छनि जे दशकों सं नारायणी नदी के बदलैत रस्ता के कारण सीमा आओर जटिल भ गेल अछि.

रविदिन के घटना ३१ मई के सेहो एहने विवाद के बाद भेल छल, जखन भारत के एसएसबी सुस्ता ग्रामीण नगरपालिका के वार्ड ५ मे प्रवेश केलक आ नेपाल के ऊर्जा, जल संसाधन आ सिंचाई मंत्रालय द्वारा बनाओल जा रहल स्थायी तटबंध के निर्माण पर आपत्ति केलक।

मुख्य जिल्ला अधिकारी नेपालके अनुसार विवाद एक विद्यमान संरचनाके लगभग ५० मिटर पूर्वमे योजनाबद्ध १३२ मिटरके नयाँ तटबन्धखण्डमे केन्द्रित छल, जे अखनो नेपाली क्षेत्रमे अछि ।

ई परियोजना तत्कालीन ऊर्जा मंत्री कुलमान घिसिंग के करीब आठ महीना पहिने सुस्ता के दौरा के बाद शुरू करलौ गेलौ छेलै आरू अधिकारियौ क कमजोर बस्ती लेली बाढ़ सुरक्षा क प्राथमिकता दै के निर्देश देलकै ।

सुस्ता के उत्तर आ पश्चिम में नारायणी नदी आ दक्षिण आ पूर्व में भारत के बिहार राज्य अछि |

भारत एहि क्षेत्रक समीप तीनटा एसएसबी चौकी रखैत अछि, जखन कि नेपाल मे एकटा निरीक्षक क कमान मे एपीएफ सीमा चौकी अछि।

निवासी सब के कहनाय छनि जे भारतीय अधिकारी बेर-बेर एहि इलाका मे नेपाल के गतिविधि पर आपत्ति जतौलनि अछि, जाहि मे स्पष्ट रूप सं सीमांकित सीमा स्तंभ के अभाव के हवाला देल गेल अछि.

दू सप्ताह पहिने सुस्ता अभियानी मुन्ना खान के नेतृत्व मे 52 निवासी काठमांडू जा क मैतीघर मंडला मे विरोध प्रदर्शन केने छलाह, जाहि मे राज्य के मजबूत संरक्षण के मांग कायल गेल छल।

गृहमन्त्री सूडान गुरुङसँग बैसारमे भारतीय सुरक्षाकर्मीद्वारा वर्षोसँ उत्पीड़नके आरोप लगाबैत सुस्तामे नेपाली सेनाके सुरक्षा चौकी स्थापना करबाक आग्रह कएलनि ।

बैठक के बाद गृह मंत्रालय न॑ जिला प्रशासन क॑ निर्देश देलकै कि सुस्ता के संवेदनशील क्षेत्रऽ म॑ सुरक्षा क॑ मजबूत करलऽ जाय आरू नागरिकता के दस्तावेज के कमी वाला पात्र निवासी लेली नागरिकता आवेदन के प्रक्रिया शुरू करलऽ जाय ।

Key Takeaways:

Phur Galjen Sherpa summited Gasherbrum I (8,080m) on Aug 1

He completed all 14 eight-thousanders, joining an elite global club

Record includes 20 Everest summits and rare climbs like Nanga Parbat in autumn

Also summited Yalung Kang (8,505m) in 2004, bringing his tally to 15 peaks

Phur Galjen Sherpa has officially joined the elite club of climbers who have summited all 14 eight-thousanders, completing his quest with a successful ascent of Gasherbrum I (8,080m) in Pakistan on August 1. Remarkably, the summit came just eleven days after he climbed Gasherbrum II on July 21, confirmed Mingma G, Managing Director of Imagine Nepal Treks.

Related Articles Nepal's Kili Pemba Sherpa completes all 14 world's highest peaks with Nanga Parbat ascent Pasang Sona Sherpa sets rare Everest record with three ascents via three routes in under a year

Phur Galjen Sherpa, a native of Thame village in Solukhumbu, began his climbing career as a local Sherpa in 1997 and achieved his first Everest summit in 1999. Over the years, he has built an extraordinary record, summiting all 14 of the world's eight-thousanders: Everest 20 times; K2 twice; Kanchenjunga once (2018); Lhotse, Cho Oyu, Annapurna, and Makalu twice each; Manaslu and Broad Peak three times each; and single ascents of Shishapangma, Dhaulagiri, and Nanga Parbat - the latter including the first autumn ascent of the peak in 2017. Most recently, he added Gasherbrum I and Gasherbrum II to his tally.

Beyond the 14 official 8,000-meter peaks, Imagine Nepal noted that Phur Galjen also summited Yalung Kang (8,505m) in 2004, a feat achieved by only five Nepali climbers - bringing his total to 15 distinct 8,000-meter-plus summits.

Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke has rejected comparisons between his group's recent student protest in Delhi and the upheavals in Bangladesh and Nepal, saying Indian students should draw inspiration from Mahatma Gandhi instead.

In an interview to PTI, Dipke defended the protest over alleged exam irregularities and insisted that the demonstrators had followed the Constitution and maintained peace despite police action.

Rejecting remarks by exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen linking the Delhi protest to the 2024 agitation in Bangladesh that led to the fall of Sheikh Hasina's Awami League government, Dipke said India did not need to look outside for models of protest.

Dipke said some people may have drawn parallels with protests in Bangladesh and Nepal because of the police action during the Delhi demonstration.

"The students in India were not violent or aggressive. They got their heads, arms and legs broken but displayed restraint and sat peacefully at Jantar Mantar," he said.

He also argued that education should become a central issue in electoral politics.

"If you don't make education the main agenda in election, it means you are not thinking about the future. Education is an investment for the future of the country," Dipke said.

DEMAND FOR NEET VICTIMS' COMPENSATION

Dipke criticised the government over what he described as a delay in compensation to families of NEET aspirants who died by suicide.

"They have money to topple government overnight. You can buy MPs and MLAs by spending hundreds of crores of rupees, but when it comes to the NEET victims and their kin, they look at the norms," he said.

He warned that CJP could launch another agitation if its demands were not addressed.

"The government should meet our demands as soon as possible, or else we will launch another agitation," he said.

Dipke also urged Gen Z protesters to maintain restraint and not imitate the conduct of politicians.

He said young protesters should "not reach the level of BJP leaders" who, according to him, abuse even in Parliament and at public rallies.

"There is some difference between us and the goons and that difference should always be there," he said.

SUPPORT FOR JHARKHAND STUDENTS

Dipke extended CJP's support to students protesting in Jharkhand over alleged irregularities in the state public service examination and other recruitment tests.

He backed their demand for a CBI probe and reforms in recruitment agencies, saying the movement was against the system rather than any political party.

"Their fight is not against any political party but against the system. We stand with their demands. If they want a CBI probe, we are going to support them in pursuing that," he said.

He said CJP would support student movements over education and recruitment issues irrespective of which party was in power.

"Wherever agitations will happen for education and wherever students come forward to demand their rights, we are going to stand with them, irrespective of the ruling party in that state," Dipke said.

"The rules are the same as our fight is not against any political party. It is against the system that has let down the students of the country," he added.

OPPOSITION LEADERS' SUPPORT

Asked about opposition leaders who visited Jantar Mantar to support the student protest, Dipke said they did not use the platform for political promotion.

"Everyone was sensitive towards the students' agitation. They were very sensitive towards the cause and the students. When they were on the stage at Jantar Mantar, none of these leaders spoke about their political party, but said they were there to support the students," he said.

CJP PLANS EXPANSION

Dipke said CJP would discuss its future roadmap at a meeting at his residence in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on August 5.

Around 10 to 15 people are expected to attend the meeting, with other volunteers also expected to play a role in expanding the movement.

"The expansion of CJP will take place. Our responsibility has increased after the success of the recent protest. People's expectations about CJP have also gone up. In the meeting on Wednesday, we will discuss our future roadmap," Dipke said.

Dipke also criticised what he described as the gap between India's education system and those in other countries, particularly in infrastructure and practical learning.

"The biggest difference is that foreign countries have a good infrastructure when it comes to education," he said.

Drawing on his own experience in the US, Dipke said courses there were more practical and less theoretical, and argued that India needed to create greater scope for practical learning.

He also claimed that the present government was spending less on education than the previous regime.

"The maximum funds should go towards education. There is no dearth of funds with the government, so I don't understand why they are reducing expenditure on education. Education is something where the maximum spending should take place as it is the foundation of a nation," he said.

"We don't know how much money there is in the PM Cares Fund. I think the education department could really take some help from that fund," he added.

Dipke said education had become unaffordable and inaccessible for many people in India and called for greater government spending on the sector.

full_article:
Nepal’s national identity infrastructure has seen extensive technical failures, leaving thousands unable to access services that are verified through the National Identity Management Information System (NIDMIS).

Since early July, 13 government agencies including the Department of Passports, banks, tax offices and immigration have suffered authentication problems via National Identity Numbers (NINs). Official departments have been forced to manually accept confirmation pages as a temporary workaround, reports The Kathmandu Post.

The Department of National ID and Civil Registration said new applicants were receiving NINs but their records were not being approved by the system, leading to widespread complaints. The department’s director general Krishna Poudel said IT teams, supported by French vendor IN Groupe, had been working for a week to restore functionality.

IN Groupe supplied both NIDMIS and Nepal’s Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS), and has now deployed specialists to Kathmandu, with officials expecting full restoration next week. Only two weeks ago, it was revealed that Nepali authorities had chosen IN Groupe for a new ABIS with the system upgraded for a capacity of 10 million biometric records.

The agreement seemed to have been struck with some urgency, as The Kathmandu Post reported the direct procurement bypassed normal tender procedures, allowed by the Public Procurement Act, and the license of the ABIS was said to have been nearing expiry with capacity left for only a few thousand data entries.

The outage leaves further questions as the government on May 8 cancelled a global tender for long‑term operation and maintenance of NIDMIS, choosing to manage the system in‑house instead. The government cited a push for digital sovereignty, even as it was reported technical evaluation was not completed before the tender was cancelled.

Reliance on national ID magnifies impact

Nepal has collected biometric data from around 20 million people, but only 7.8 million national identity cards have been printed, leaving millions waiting. Officials warn that delays are worsening as the card becomes mandatory for passports, banking, social security, driving licences, property transactions and university entrance exams.

The national identity card is now mandatory to conduct transactions using Nepal’s national digital payment system. The country’s central bank issued an amendment to this effect, with the aim of strengthening eKYC for all financial operations.

Nepal officials have formally lodged a proposal with Indian authorities requesting that its NID card be recognized as an official travel document, giving it the same status as passports. Nepal’s immigration director Ram Chandra Tiwari said the eventual aim was to replace citizenship certificates, which can also be used as travel documents for India, with the NIN entirely.

But this could all be stymied if the back-end infrastructure is not in place. Agencies linked to NIDMIS say they have repeatedly raised concerns about the slow response. Some have reported severe service backlogs, particularly at the Department of Passports, which has seen a surge in applicants following new migration labor openings in South Korea.

Banks have also been unable to update KYC records because national identity numbers cannot be verified. For now, the affected agencies have been instructed to continue providing services using enrollment confirmation pages until authentication is restored.

The disruption has drawn fresh concerns about Nepal’s ability to manage one of its largest digital infrastructure projects without external support. Earlier this year, the World Bank approved US$50 million to finance the build of digital public infrastructure with the funding going towards digital platforms and a new national identity system.

Nepal’s government has since argued that domestic control will strengthen data sovereignty, but officials inside the department claim they lack the expertise to recover from major failures.

title: 25% of Nepali Removal Orders Over 28 Years Issued Under Trump in 18 Months; Relief-Grant Rate Falls to 7.6% - nepyork

full_article:
In just 18 months, U.S. immigration courts issued 1,162 removal orders to Nepali nationals between January 2025 and June 2026—accounting for 25% of all removal orders recorded for the group over the past 28 years, according to Executive Office for Immigration Review records compiled by TRAC.

When combined with Donald Trump’s first presidential term, courts have issued a total of 2,006 removal orders to Nepali nationals across both terms, representing 43.24% of the 4,639 total removal orders recorded in the dataset since 1998. In fiscal year 2025 and the first nine months of fiscal year 2026, removal orders remained the dominant outcome in the Nepal docket, far outpacing grants of relief and case closures.

Relief Granted at 7.6%

For fiscal year 2025, the data show 1,837 total case hearings involving Nepalis. Of those, judges issued 569 removal orders and granted relief in 378 cases—which represents 20.58% of total hearings. Additionally, 249 cases were terminated, and 223 were recorded as “no Notice to Appear (NTA) filed.”

Other outcomes included 185 credible-fear cases in which fear was not found, 94 credible-fear cases in which fear was found, 87 voluntary departures, and 23 other closures. Smaller categories included 13 “credible-fear other” cases, 11 “withholding-only other” cases, two prosecutorial-discretion outcomes, two “asylum-only other” cases, and one “withholding-only” case not granted.

Removal orders were the single largest outcome in fiscal year 2025, followed by grants of relief and terminations. Grants accounted for just over one in five total outcomes (20.58%), or 39.92% of direct merits decisions.

For the first nine months of fiscal year 2026, the Nepal docket recorded 941 total case hearings through the reporting period. Judges issued 634 removal orders, while 88 cases were terminated, 73 ended in voluntary departure, and 72 resulted in grants of relief, representing 7.65% of total hearings. Other outcomes included 30 credible-fear cases in which fear was not found, 29 “no NTA filed” cases, six other closures, five credible-fear cases in which fear was found, three “credible-fear other” cases, and one asylum-only case in which relief was not granted.

The fiscal year 2026 figures show an even more removal-heavy outcome mix than fiscal year 2025. Removal orders accounted for the clear majority of resolved cases, while grants of relief fell to a much smaller share of the docket—accounting for just 7.65% of total outcomes and 10.20% of direct merits decisions.

Removal orders for Nepali nationals in U.S. immigration courts rose sharply in fiscal years 2025 and 2026, according to Executive Office for Immigration Review records compiled by TRAC.

The pace of removal orders for Nepali nationals has climbed dramatically in the most recent period. Judges issued 1,162 removal orders between January 2025 and June 2026, representing more than a quarter of the total recorded over 28 years and far exceeding the totals registered under the Biden administration and Trump’s first term.

In calendar year 2025 alone, judges issued 783 removal orders for Nepali nationals, with the monthly total rising from 26 in January to a high of 112 in October. In the first six months of calendar year 2026, immigration judges issued another 379 removal orders, keeping the monthly pace at an average of nearly 63 orders.

Judges issued 644 removal orders for Nepali nationals during the Biden administration, from January 2021 through December 2024, and 864 during Trump’s first term, from January 2017 through December 2020. The 2025 total alone exceeded the four-year Biden total.

Historical Relief Grant and Removal Trends

At the same time, relief grant totals for Nepali nationals have been volatile over the long term and notably lower in the most recent year. Courts recorded 720 grants of relief in 2023—the highest annual total on record—followed by 607 in 2024, before a sharp drop to 378 in 2025 and 72 in 2026. While courts were issuing more removal orders in 2025 and 2026, they were granting relief at a far lower rate than during the 2023 peak.

The grant-of-relief pattern has fluctuated widely over time. Totals were 14 in 1998, 35 in 2001, 41 in 2002, 65 in 2003, 103 in 2004, and 96 in 2005 before rising to 180 in 2006 and 189 in 2009. Relief grants later climbed to 251 in 2010, 343 in 2011, 436 in 2012, and 445 in 2013, holding in the 300s through much of the mid-2010s before peaking in 2023.

Relief grants for Nepali nationals rose and fell over time, reaching 720 in 2023 before dropping to 378 in 2025 and 72 in 2026, according to TRAC-compiled EOIR records.

A fiscal-year view of the removal-order data reveals a similar upward trend, with 569 removal orders in fiscal year 2025 and 634 in fiscal year 2026, both well above earlier peaks. Those totals outpaced previous high-water marks, such as 349 in fiscal year 2019, 237 in fiscal year 2011, 218 in fiscal year 2018, and 204 in fiscal year 2023.

Removal orders for Nepali nationals were relatively modest in the late 1990s and early 2000s before gradually rising. The dataset includes 28 orders in 1998, 42 in 1999, 50 in 2000, 31 in 2001, 34 in 2002, 49 in 2003, and 66 in 2004. Orders then climbed to 94 in 2005, 95 in 2006, 88 in 2007, and 100 in 2008.

The numbers increased further in the 2010s, with 122 in 2009, 129 in 2010, 237 in 2011, 180 in 2012, 183 in 2013, 187 in 2014, 127 in 2015, 107 in 2016, 139 in 2017, 218 in 2018, and 349 in 2019. The total dipped to 170 in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic before rising again to 48 in 2021, 163 in 2022, 204 in 2023, and 196 in 2024, leading up to the sharp jump in 2025 and 2026.

The 783 orders in 2025 alone were more than four times the total from 2024 and nearly double the combined totals from 2021 and 2022.

वित्तीय वर्ष 2026 क पहिल नौ मास लेल नेपाल डॉकेट मे रिपोर्टिंग अवधि क माध्यम स कुल 941 मामला क सुनवाई दर्ज कैल गेल। जज सब 634 हटाबय के आदेश जारी केलनि, जखन कि 88 मामला समाप्त भ गेल, 73 स्वैच्छिक प्रस्थान मे समाप्त भेल, आ 72 के परिणामस्वरूप राहत के अनुदान भेटल, जे कुल सुनवाई के 7.65% के प्रतिनिधित्व करैत अछि. अन्य परिणामऽ म॑ ३० विश्वसनीय-भय के मामला शामिल छेलै जेकरा म॑ डर नै मिललै, २९ “कोय एनटीए दायर नै करलऽ गेलऽ” केस, छह अन्य बंदी, ५ विश्वसनीय-डर केस जेकरा म॑ डर मिललै, तीन “विश्वसनीय-डर केस अन्य” मामला, आरू एक शरण-मात्र मामला जेकरा म॑ राहत नै देलऽ गेलऽ छेलै ।

नेपाली नागरिक के हटाबै के आदेश के गति सबसें ताजा अवधि में भारी बढ़ोत्तरी होय गेलऽ छै । जज न॑ जनवरी २०२५ आरू जून २०२६ के बीच १,१६२ हटाबै के आदेश जारी करलकै, जे २८ साल म॑ दर्ज कुल के एक चौथाई स॑ भी अधिक के प्रतिनिधित्व करै छै आरू बाइडेन प्रशासन आरू ट्रंप केरऽ पहलऽ कार्यकाल के तहत दर्ज कुल आदेश स॑ बहुत अधिक छै ।

ऐतिहासिक राहत अनुदान एवं हटाने के प्रवृत्ति
